P1.evidence: No setter suffix on the title and no application or setter notes were read back, so P1a is unreachable. The frame was two-part, not four: 'let's just get super clear on where you are, right? Where you want to be. If I feel like we can help you, great.' — no 'what's in the way' and no 'what you need'. Agreement was sought only as a tossed-off 'Alrighty? Okay.' Open question ran clean: 'in your opinion, what is it that you feel like we might be able to help you with, man?'

P2.evidence: Health and injury baseline was the strongest part: 'What's the health issue, if you don't mind me asking?' and 'what about the injuries? What injuries do you have?' plus a good frequency probe. Diet covered: 'how would you say your nutrition is? Can you walk me through that'. But age was never asked; height and weight were volunteered ('I'm five, five, five, six, a hundred [fifty]') off the back of the rep echoing 'you said you're the heaviest you've ever been'. Occupation never asked — the prospect volunteered 'I work two jobs' and only revealed 'I'm a psychotherapist' at 00:40:16, after the call was effectively over. Sleep and daytime energy were never raised at all. Results from current training volunteered, not asked.

P3.evidence: Best-run phase. Strong bridge to the deeper driver: 'what's kind of had you wanting to now... There must have been a shift of some sort of perspective'. Excellent 10-out-of-10 probe — 'let's say you perform at your best a 10 out of 10, what does that actually look like? What's different from where you're at now?' — which produced the mobility/strength/endurance answer. Drove hard through to legacy and identity: 'What is the example you want to set?' Clean reflect-back at 00:12:55: 'it sounds like the weight number isn't much of an issue... it's more about almost like a come-to-Jesus moment... Does that make sense?' The son was volunteered unprompted at 00:02:51, not surfaced by a 'who else does that impact' question, so P3f scores miss under the volunteered-information rule.

P4.evidence: Asked the coaching-history question directly: 'have you had a coach before with your fitness or a personal trainer or anything like that?' Ran a strong structural version of P4f: 'God could come down and make the best program in the world, but if you don't do it because of XYZ reason, it doesn't matter how good the program is. What do you feel like needs to change internally for you to really go and get what you want?' The prospect named his own gap — 'what needs to happen is I need to build healthy habits'. 'Why do you feel it didn't stick' was never asked as such; the outcome of the self-directed kettlebell block was volunteered ('I would choose the same workouts... I wouldn't go through the whole bank').

P5.evidence: The consequence frame was gestured at but never run. The rep quoted 'if nothing changes, nothing changes' at 00:18:54 and moved straight to the root-cause question — he never asked what the next two years look like if nothing changes, never asked whether that is acceptable, never asked why not, and never asked for a line in the sand. The only cost-of-inaction language arrived after the price landed ('I know if you don't then you'll be in the same [place]'), by which point it read as rebuttal rather than frame.

P6.evidence: P6a ran: 'Most important thing, do you feel like we can actually help you? ... do you feel like we can actually get you to where you want to be?' But the answer was soft — 'I mean, I think so. I've never done anything like this that's so comprehensive' — and the rep proceeded to numbers anyway rather than returning to Phase 5. P6b was never asked in any form, which is the pivotal omission: the prospect had already named price as the sole blocker at 00:19:45 and the rep deliberately parked it — 'I wasn't talking about in the context of moving forward with this, by the way' — instead of isolating it before presenting.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted but the prospect declined at the number, so no payment, onboarding booking, agreement email or welcome-email walkthrough was reachable. The rep did pre-frame the Trevor onboarding call and the 24-48 hour build before quoting ('we're going to book in your onboarding call with Trevor. We'd do it for Monday'), but nothing was actually scheduled.

objection_plays.detail: Isolation ran, but late and in the wrong order — the price landed first, and only at 00:31:45 did the rep ask 'money aside, do you feel like it can get you where you want to go?', by which point the prospect had already decided. The 'break it up' move was offered ('we can break it up if you need to. Like, we don't want money to get in the way') but never structured. Zero of the six FINANCIAL PICTURE moves ran: no cash on hand, no monthly surplus after bills, no credit card count, no available credit, no used-vs-available, no investments. The rep instead improvised a three-month / $4,000 tier and then pivoted to resourcefulness pressure ('if you had to pay for a surgery for somebody, and it was 6k, you'd find it'), which is not in the play.

Trigger was substantive — 'me going to her and say, hey, babe, I'm going to spend 6k... she doesn't even know I'm on this call'. The rep ran the framing move well and ran a variant of 'is this genuinely needing her input, or asking permission to bet on yourself' as 'it sounds like you're not sure more so than her though'. But he skipped 'money aside, do you personally feel this CAN get you to your goal' at the point the spouse objection surfaced, never asked 'is there any reason she would NOT want you stronger and less in pain', never ran the joint-decision/responsibility move, and never offered the deposit-plus-refund fallback.

The real objection was household liquidity in a two-job NYC family with childcare and school costs — a genuine inability to fund $6,000, not reluctance. The playbook has no path for this: OC assumes latent capacity to pay and its only tools are instalments and financial interrogation. With no lower legitimate tier and no structured plan, the rep was left with resourcefulness pressure, which converted a warm, high-belief prospect into a loss. This is a script gap, not solely a rep failure.

notes: Two fixable errors decided this call. First, the prospect handed over the blocker at 00:19:45 — 'the only thing honestly that would stand in the way is the price' — and the rep waved it off instead of qualifying budget or isolating it then; had he run P6b there, the whole back half changes. Second, P5 was skipped entirely, so the number arrived with no cost-of-inaction built behind it. Discovery and the deep-why work (P3, P4) were genuinely strong — the son, jiu-jitsu-as-barometer and the habits gap were all surfaced cleanly — which makes the process failure downstream, not upstream. Coach on: qualify budget before presenting, run P5 before P6, and stop inventing tiers under price pressure.
